Binding for all projects in this folder (corpus.md). Echo tags follow guidelines §6.4: [cognate], [equivalent], [divergence], [absent]. Fixed 2026-10-17 by the corpus coordinator before drafting project 1 (Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty, EST); the EST-only formulas are in 1-אמנת-הירושה-של-אסרחדון/renderings.md.

The danger specific to this corpus. Deuteronomy's vocabulary (בְּרִית, אָלָה, שָׁמַר, שָׁמַע, אָהַב, בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ, נָבִיא, לֹא תֹסֵף … וְלֹא תִגְרַע) is the natural Hebrew for much of what the treaties say, so a translator can make the treaty sound like Deuteronomy without noticing it. On the other hand, real cognates (נָצַר, שָׁמַע, אָרַר, חָטָא, נֶפֶשׁ, שִׁנָּה, מֵישָׁרִים, נָסַח) must stay visible. Hence: each Deuteronomic key word is used only where the Akkadian has its cognate or its exact equivalent, and every use is tagged.

0. Inheritance

The flood corpus's shared renderings (../סיפורי-המבול-המסופוטמיים/renderings.md) and the creation corpus's (../סיפורי-הבריאה-המסופוטמיים/renderings.md, especially §3 and §5) are binding here as the default. The items most needed in treaties and laws:

Akkadian Hebrew Note
ilu, ilū (NA ilāni), iltu; ilāni rabûtu אֵל, אֵלִים, אֵלָה; הָאֵלִים הַגְּדוֹלִים Never אֱלֹהִים.
šamû; erṣetu; mātu; qaqqaru (NA kaqqiru) שָׁמַיִם; אֶרֶץ; אֶרֶץ; קַרְקַע NA šamû u kaqqiru "heaven and earth" = שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ (the merism; note that the Akkadian word is kaqqiru); elsewhere kaqqiru = קַרְקַע [cognate]. Never אֲדָמָה.
šarru; šarrūtu; bēlu; bēlūtu מֶלֶךְ; מַלְכוּת; אָדוֹן; אֲדָנוּת
šīmtu; šīmta šâmu; ana šīmti alāku גּוֹרָל; גָּזַר גּוֹרָל; הָלַךְ לְגוֹרָלוֹ "to go to one's fate" = to die.
ṭuppu לוּחַ
šumu; zēru; šuma zakāru שֵׁם; זֶרַע; הִזְכִּיר שֵׁם (N: נִזְכַּר שְׁמוֹ) [cognate] / [cognate] / [cognate]
napištu נֶפֶשׁ (or חַיִּים when the sense demands, with a note) [cognate]
libbu לֵב [cognate]. ina libbi (NA "in, into, from") is a preposition: בְּ־, בְּתוֹךְ, מִתּוֹךְ, not "in the heart".
ṭābu; damqu; banû (adj.) טוֹב; נָאֶה; יָפֶה טוֹב only for ṭābu (creation corpus). So lā ṭābtu lā deʾiqtu = לֹא טוֹבָה, לֹא נָאָה; lā banītu = לֹא יָפָה.
lemnu; lemuttu רַע; רָעָה
šīru; damu; eṣemtu; pagru בָּשָׂר; דָּם; עֶצֶם; פֶּגֶר [equivalent]; [cognate]; [cognate]; [cognate]
eṭemmu אִט (pl. אִטִּים), always vocalized Isa 19:3.
akalu; mû; karānu לֶחֶם; מַיִם; יַיִן [cognate] (akalu, mû) / [equivalent].
bubūtu רָעָב
kupru כֹּפֶר [cognate] (Gen 6:14).
abūbu מַבּוּל [equivalent].
arāru; arratu (erretu) אָרַר; מְאֵרָה [cognate] ↔ אָרוּר (דברים כז:טו–כו; כח:טז–יט), הַמְּאֵרָה (דברים כח:כ). Only arāru is אָרַר.
ana ūmī ṣâti; ana ūmī dārûti לִימֵי עַד; לִימֵי נֶצַח Never לְעוֹלָם (creation corpus).
qabû; dabābu אָמַר; דִּבֵּר
amātu / NA abutu "word, matter" דָּבָר
ṣalmu צֶלֶם [cognate]
Šamaš (god) / šamšu (sun) שַׁמַשׁ / שֶׁמֶשׁ, vocalized at every occurrence where both occur
nabû (name) קָרָא Reserved, as in the creation corpus.
šakānu שָׂם (vocalized) As in the creation corpus (reserved for this verb).

1. Proper names (shared)

Akkadian Hebrew Note
Aššur (the god) אַשּׁוּר Same spelling as the land; the first occurrence notes the double use ("the god Aššur, of the land Aššur").
Mat-Aššur (the land) אַשּׁוּר (אֶרֶץ אַשּׁוּר where the Akkadian has māt in a construct phrase that needs it) Biblical form.
Anu; Illil / Enlil; Ea אָנוּ; אֶנְלִיל; אֵאָה Flood corpus.
Sîn; Šamaš; Adad; Marduk; Nabû סִין; שַׁמַשׁ; אֲדַד; מַרְדּוּךְ; נָבוּ Marduk: note מְרֹדָךְ (ירמיהו נ:ב); Nabû: note נְבוֹ (ישעיהו מו:א). Not assimilated.
Nergal; Ninurta; Nusku; Uraš נֵרְגַל; נִינוּרְתָּה; נוּסְכּוּ; אוּרַשׁ Nergal in the biblical form (מלכים ב יז:ל), as in the creation corpus.
Mullissu (Mulliltu) = Ninlil; Šerua; Bēlet-ilī מוּלִּיסּוּ (מוּלִּלְתּוּ where the text has the SB form); שֵׁרוּעָה; בֵּלֶת־אִילִי
Ištar (of Nineveh, of Arbela) אִשְׁתַּר (שֶׁל נִינְוֵה, שֶׁל אַרְבֵּאִיל) Never עַשְׁתֹּרֶת.
Gula; Girra; Palil; Zarpanītu; Sebetti גּוּלָה; גִּירָּה; פָּלִיל; צַרְפָּנִיתוּ; הַשִּׁבְעָה (Sebetti, "the Seven", note)
Esarhaddon (Aššur-aḫu-iddina) אֵסַרְחַדּוֹן (plain: אסרחדון) Decision (open for the user): kings named in the Bible get the biblical form, as places do: אֵסַר־חַדֹּן (מלכים ב יט:לז; עזרא ד:ב), written as one word as in modern Hebrew. The first occurrence notes the Akkadian name "Aššur gave a brother".
Sennacherib (Sîn-aḫḫē-erība) סַנְחֵרִיב Biblical (מלכים ב יח:יג).
Assurbanipal (Aššur-bāni-apli) אַשּׁוּר־בָּנִי־אַפְלִי (plain: אשור־בני־אפלי) Akkadian form, as in the creation corpus (KAR 4 colophon); the biblical אָסְנַפַּר (עזרא ד:י) is a probable but not certain identification and unfamiliar: note only.
Šamaš-šumu-ukīn שַׁמַשׁ־שׁוּם־אוּכִּין
Places: Nineveh; Kalḫu; Ḫarrān; Babylon; Akkad; Arbela; Borsippa; Nippur; Carchemish; Kunalia (Tayinat) נִינְוֵה; כֶּלַח; חָרָן; בָּבֶל; אַכַּד; אַרְבֵּאִיל; בּוֹרְסִפָּה; נִיפּוּר; כַּרְכְּמִישׁ; כּוּנַלְיָה (note: = כַלְנֵה (עמוס ו:ב), כַּלְנוֹ (ישעיהו י:ט)) Biblical forms for biblical places (כֶּלַח, בראשית י:יא; חָרָן, בראשית יא:לא; כַּרְכְּמִישׁ, ישעיהו י:ט, ירמיהו מו:ב). Kunalia is not certainly the same place as Calneh: keep the Akkadian form and note.
Sumer and Akkad שׁוּמֶר וְאַכַּד

2. Treaty, oath and loyalty terms (with echo tags)

Akkadian Hebrew Rejected Echo Reason
adê (pl. tantum; Aram. ʿdy / ʿdn, Sefire) "treaty, loyalty oath" אֲמָנָה (sg. in Hebrew: adê annûti = הָאֲמָנָה הַזֹּאת); ṭuppi adê = לוּחַ הָאֲמָנָה; ina adê erēbu = בָּא בָּאֲמָנָה בְּרִית (would make every stipulation sound like Deuteronomy's covenant and pre-empt the comparison); עֵדוּת / עֵדֹת (a possible but debated cognate: Aram. ʿdy, Heb. עֵדֹת, דברים ד:מה; ו:יז, כ; לֻחֹת הָעֵדֻת, שמות לא:יח; it is not certain, and עֵדֹת would read as "testimonies"); אָלָה (that is māmītu); שְׁבוּעָה (that is tamītu) [equivalent] בְּרִית (דברים כט:ח, יא, יג); [cognate?] עֵדֹת, לֻחֹת הָעֵדֻת (debated) אֲמָנָה (נחמיה י:א) is the neutral Hebrew word for a binding, written, sworn agreement, and it is the word modern Hebrew uses for such treaties. It pre-empts nothing in the Torah, and it lets the apparatus show both candidate echoes: Deuteronomy's לוּחֹת הַבְּרִית (דברים ט:ט) and Exodus's לֻחֹת הָעֵדֻת beside ṭuppi adê. Open decision for the user (project 1 project.md): אֲמָנָה or עֵדֹת.
māmītu "oath (as a binding curse)"; māmīta tamû "swear an oath"; māmīta pašāru "release (an) oath" אָלָה; נִשְׁבַּע אָלָה; הִתִּיר אָלָה שְׁבוּעָה (reserved for tamītu) [equivalent] אָלָה (דברים כט:יא, יג, יח–כ; יחזקאל יז:יג, טז, יח–יט) Deviation from the creation corpus (there Sum. nam-erim₂ / Akk. māmītu = שְׁבוּעָה), because EST distinguishes two oath words: tamītu (from tamû "swear") and māmītu (the oath as the curse that seizes the perjurer, "an māmītu that cannot be released", l. 433). Hebrew אָלָה is exactly the oath-curse (בִּשְׁבֻעַת הָאָלָה, במדבר ה:כא).
tamû "swear"; tamītu "oath"; tamû D "make swear" נִשְׁבַּע; שְׁבוּעָה; הִשְׁבִּיעַ [equivalent] The noun follows its verb in both languages. 2 Kgs 11:4 וַיַּשְׁבַּע אֹתָם … וַיַּרְא אֹתָם אֶת בֶּן הַמֶּלֶךְ is the closest biblical scene (a succession oath for a crown prince).
naṣāru "guard, keep, protect"; maṣṣartu "watch, guard duty, observance" נָצַר; נְצִירָה (maṣṣarta naṣāru = נָצַר נְצִירָה) שָׁמַר; מִשְׁמֶרֶת / מִשְׁמָר (root שמר) [cognate] נָצַר ↔ וּבְרִיתְךָ יִנְצֹרוּ (דברים לג:ט); [equivalent] Deuteronomy's שָׁמַר (דברים ד:ב, ו; יג:א, ה, יט) נָצַר everywhere for naṣāru (the cognate, and the creation corpus's rendering), never שָׁמַר: the reader sees that Deuteronomy's usual שָׁמַר is not the treaty's verb, while Deut 33:9 has the very cognate. maṣṣartu gets a transparent noun of the same root, נְצִירָה (note at the first occurrence).
šemû "hear, listen, obey" שָׁמַע [cognate] ↔ כִּי תִשְׁמַע (דברים יג:יג); לֹא תִשְׁמַע אֶל דִּבְרֵי הַנָּבִיא (דברים יג:ד); שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל (דברים ו:ד) The real cognate: keep it visible.
râmu (NA raʾāmu) "love" אָהַב רָחַם (Hebrew "have pity") [equivalent] ↔ וְאָהַבְתָּ (דברים ו:ה); הֲיִשְׁכֶם אֹהֲבִים (דברים יג:ד); 1 Sam 18:1, 3 וַיֶּאֱהָבֵהוּ … כְּנַפְשׁוֹ The natural Hebrew for "love"; Moran 1963 made this the classic case of treaty "love" = loyalty. Note at the first occurrence that râmu is often compared with West Semitic rḥm (אֶרְחָמְךָ, תהלים יח:ב; Aram. "love"); not certain. kī napšatkunu "as your own life" = כְּנַפְשְׁכֶם [cognate] (רֵעֲךָ אֲשֶׁר כְּנַפְשְׁךָ, דברים יג:ז; כְּנַפְשׁוֹ, שמואל א יח:א).
ramû D (NA rammû) "let go, abandon" הִרְפָּה (מִן) עָזַב (reserved for ezēbu) [equivalent] ↔ לֹא יַרְפְּךָ וְלֹא יַעַזְבֶךָּ (דברים לא:ו, ח) False friend of râmu: turammâni (§96, l. 634) is "you abandon", not "you love".
ezēbu עָזַב [cognate]
ḫaṭû "sin, offend, transgress (against)"; ḫīṭu "sin" חָטָא (בְּ־); חֵטְא [cognate] ina adê ḫaṭû = חָטָא בָּאֲמָנָה.
šanû D (šunnû) "change, alter" שִׁנָּה [cognate] ↔ דברים יג:א [divergence]: the treaty forbids altering the king's word or the tablet; Deuteronomy forbids adding and subtracting (לֹא תֹסֵף … וְלֹא תִגְרַע, also ד:ב). Levinson 2010.
enû "change, revoke, alter" הֵמִיר [equivalent] ↔ לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ וְלֹא יָמִיר (ויקרא כז:י) Paired with šunnû (תָּמִירוּ, תְּשַׁנּוּ).
nakāru D "remove, depose, alter" הֵסִיר נִכֵּר (Heb. "recognize") [equivalent] ina šarrūti nukkuru = הֵסִיר מִן הַמַּלְכוּת.
pašāṭu "erase" מָחָה פָּשַׁט (cognate in form, but Hebrew "strip") [equivalent] ↔ וּמָחָה יְהוָה אֶת שְׁמוֹ (דברים כט:יט); וְאֶמְחֶה אֶת שְׁמָם (דברים ט:יד)
ḫulluqu (D of ḫalāqu) "make disappear, destroy"; ḫalāqu G "disappear, perish"; ḫalāqu G "flee, escape" (of persons) אִבֵּד; אָבַד; נִמְלַט (part 2, l. 178) [equivalent] ↔ וְהַאֲבַדְתָּ אֶת שְׁמָם (דברים ז:כד); אַבֵּד תְּאַבְּדוּן (דברים יב:ב); אָבֹד תֹּאבֵדוּן (דברים ד:כו)
nasāḫu "tear out, uproot" נָסַח [cognate] ↔ וְנִסַּחְתֶּם מֵעַל הָאֲדָמָה (דברים כח:סג) Flood/creation corpus cognate list.
dâku "kill"; mâtu Š (šumuttu) "put to death" הָרַג; הֵמִית [equivalent] ↔ הָרֹג תַּהַרְגֶנּוּ … לַהֲמִיתוֹ (דברים יג:י); [cognate] הֵמִית Deviation from Enūma eliš (there dâku = רָצַח, הָרַג reserved for nêru): in this corpus הָרַג is the verb of killing, and there is no nêru.
ṣabātu "seize" תָּפַשׂ [equivalent] ↔ וְתָפְשׂוּ בוֹ (דברים כא:יט)
pazzuru (D) "hide, conceal" הִסְתִּיר כִּסָּה [equivalent] ↔ וְלֹא תְכַסֶּה עָלָיו (דברים יג:ט) Not the Deuteronomic verb: let the reader see the difference.
uznā puttû "open the ears (= inform)" פָּתַח אֶת אָזְנֵי גָּלָה אֹזֶן [cognate] ↔ אֲדֹנָי יְהוִה פָּתַח לִי אֹזֶן (ישעיהו נ:ה); [equivalent] גָּלָה אֶת אֹזֶן (שמואל א ט:טו)
sīḫu "revolt"; bārtu "rebellion, conspiracy"; epēš bārti מֶרֶד; קֶשֶׁר; עָשָׂה קֶשֶׁר סָרָה [equivalent] כִּי דִבֶּר סָרָה (דברים יג:ו); קֶשֶׁר קָשֶׁר (מלכים ב יא:יד) סָרָה is kept out of the translation, so that the reader can see that Deut 13:6's word has no Akkadian cognate here.
ina gummurti libbi "with the whole heart" (lit. "in the totality of the heart") בִּשְׁלֵמוּת לִבְּכֶם (ša gummurti libbikunu = שֶׁבִּשְׁלֵמוּת לִבְּכֶם) בְּכָל לִבְּכֶם (the Deuteronomic formula, which uses כֹּל); בְּלֵב שָׁלֵם [equivalent] ↔ בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ (דברים ו:ה; יג:ד) The Akkadian noun is gummurtu "totality, completeness" (from gamāru "complete" ~ Heb. גמר). שְׁלֵמוּת keeps a noun of completeness, not Deuteronomy's כֹּל.
ina ketti (ša) libbi "in the truth of the heart" בֶּאֱמֶת לִבְּכֶם [equivalent] ↔ בֶּאֱמֶת וּבְלֵב שָׁלֵם (ישעיהו לח:ג) kittu is from kânu (כון); note it.
ša-rēši "eunuch, court official" סָרִיס [cognate] (Hebrew סָרִיס is a loan from ša rēši)
raggimu "prophet" (lit. "one who calls out"); maḫḫû "ecstatic"; mār šāʾili amat ili "inquirer of a god's word" (mār = member of the craft) נָבִיא; מְשֻׁגָּע; שׁוֹאֵל דְּבַר אֵל קוֹרֵא, מַכְרִיז (raggimu); מִתְנַבֵּא [equivalent] נָבִיא אוֹ חֹלֵם חֲלוֹם (דברים יג:ב); [equivalent] לְכָל אִישׁ מְשֻׁגָּע וּמִתְנַבֵּא (ירמיהו כט:כו; cf. מלכים ב ט:יא); [cognate] וְשֹׁאֵל אוֹב (דברים יח:יא) raggimu is the standard NA term for a prophet: the Hebrew equivalent is נָבִיא (meaning first, §6.4 rule 1), tagged, with the root difference in the note. מְשֻׁגָּע is the biblical term for the ecstatic prophet and matches maḫû "to rave": note at first occurrence that it is not "madman". šāʾilu is the cognate of שׁוֹאֵל; Weinfeld equates the šāʾilu (dream-interpreter) with חֹלֵם חֲלוֹם: note it, do not render it so.
aḫḫū mār ummi "brothers, sons of the (same) mother" אַחִים בְּנֵי אֵם (aḫḫēšu mār ummīšu = אֶחָיו בְּנֵי אִמּוֹ) [cognate] (aḫu, ummu) ↔ אָחִיךָ בֶן אִמֶּךָ (דברים יג:ז)
salmu "friend, ally" אִישׁ שְׁלוֹם (pl. אַנְשֵׁי שְׁלוֹמוֹ) בַּעַל בְּרִית [cognate] (salāmu = שלם) ↔ אִישׁ שְׁלוֹמִי (תהלים מא:י; ירמיהו כ:י)
nakru אוֹיֵב [equivalent]
ṣalmāt qaqqadi "the black-headed (people)" שְׁחוֹרֵי הָרֹאשׁ
kullumu "show, present (the crown prince)" הֶרְאָה [equivalent] ↔ וַיַּרְא אֹתָם אֶת בֶּן הַמֶּלֶךְ (מלכים ב יא:ד) Keep הֶרְאָה for this verb.
imittu u šumēlu יָמִין וּשְׂמֹאל [equivalent] / [cognate] (šumēlu = שמאל) ↔ לֹא תָסֻרוּ יָמִין וּשְׂמֹאל (דברים ה:כח); כח:יד
dīnu; diānu; kittu u mīšaru דִּין; דָּן; אֱמֶת וּמֵישָׁרִים [cognate] (dīnu, mīšaru = מֵישָׁרִים)

3. Oath grammar (binding)

Akkadian Hebrew Note
šumma attunu … (protasis of an oath stipulation) אִם אַתֶּם … The stipulation "if you do X" = "you shall not do X" (the curse is implied); "if you do not do X" (lā + verb) = "you shall do X". Keep the oath form literally: אִם אַתֶּם … לֹא תִּנְצְרוּ is also the Hebrew oath syntax (אִם = "I swear not"; אִם לֹא = "I swear that"; cf. אִם לֹא כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּמִּיתִי כֵּן הָיָתָה, ישעיהו יד:כד). Never resolve it into "you shall …".
šumma (alone) אִם
NA subjunctive -ni / -ūni / -āni in the oath clauses not rendered It marks the oath clause.
lū … lū "either … or" בֵּין … בֵּין אִם … אִם would collide with šumma.
precative li- / lu- (3rd person) jussive: יַפִּיל, יָסִיר, יְהִי
ay + preterite (negative wish) אַל + jussive (אַל יִתֵּן)
lā + present (prohibition, 2nd person) לֹא + future (לֹא תַּעֲשׂוּ) The apodictic form (as in the creation corpus).
lū + noun / stative "may it be" יְהִי / תְּהִי (יְהִי לַחְמְכֶם)
kî ša … kî hannīe "just as … so" (the simile curse) כַּאֲשֶׁר … כָּכָה כָּכָה keeps the deictic "like this" of kî hannīe (the rite was performed in front of the swearers). Deut 28:63 כַּאֲשֶׁר שָׂשׂ … כֵּן יָשִׂישׂ [equivalent].
kî (comparative "like") כְּ־
KI.MIN, KI.MIN KI.MIN (scribal "ditto", standing for the curse protasis "if you sin against this treaty …") כנ״ל / כנ״ל, כנ״ל Rendered as an abbreviation, as the scribe wrote it; the first occurrence notes what it stands for.

4. The curse vocabulary (shared; curse lists recur in all treaties and in the law epilogues)

Akkadian Hebrew Echo Note
maqātu Š "fell" הִפִּיל
akālu; Š šūkulu אָכַל; הֶאֱכִיל [cognate] ↔ לְמַאֲכָל לְכָל עוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם (דברים כח:כו)
arû; zību נֶשֶׁר; עַיִט [equivalent] ↔ דברים כח:כו (עוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם) zību "vulture" (CAD; earlier "jackal"). עַיִט (בראשית טו:יא) = bird of prey.
kalbu; šaḫû / ḫuzīru כֶּלֶב; חֲזִיר [cognate] (ḫuzīru = חזיר)
erbû אַרְבֶּה [cognate] ↔ כִּי יַחְסְלֶנּוּ הָאַרְבֶּה (דברים כח:לח)
saḫaršubbû (SAḪAR.ŠUB.BA) צָרַעַת [equivalent] ↔ בִּשְׁחִין מִצְרַיִם … וּבַגָּרָב וּבֶחָרֶס (דברים כח:כז) [divergence] The skin disease that drives its bearer out of society "like a wild ass, like a gazelle into the steppe". צָרַעַת is the Hebrew counterpart in meaning (ויקרא יג:מו); the note gives the Akkadian and Deut 28:27's terms.
eklētu; eṭû "dark" חֲשֵׁכָה; אָפֵל [equivalent] ↔ כַּאֲשֶׁר יְמַשֵּׁשׁ הָעִוֵּר בָּאֲפֵלָה (דברים כח:כט) חֲשֵׁכָה, not חֹשֶׁךְ (Gen 1:2) and not אֲפֵלָה (Deut 28:29): the reader should see the equivalence, not an identical word. eṭû "be dark" = אָפֵל (adj.) only in ūmēkunu lū eṭû.
niṭil īni "sight of the eyes" מַרְאֵה עֵינַיִם (ina niṭil īnīkunu = לְמַרְאֵה עֵינֵיכֶם) [equivalent] ↔ לְעֵינֶיךָ (דברים כח:לא–לב)
parzillu; siparru (ZABAR) בַּרְזֶל; אָרָד (2026-10-30 harmonization, was נְחֹשֶׁת; vocalized at its first occurrence in each text) [cognate] (parzillu = בַּרְזֶל, a shared culture word); [equivalent] (siparru: biblical נְחֹשֶׁת is bronze – the same metal in other words) ↔ דברים כח:כג; ויקרא כו:יט Copper (erû, URUDU) keeps נְחֹשֶׁת.
zunnu; zanānu גֶּשֶׁם; יָרַד (גֶּשֶׁם), "may it rain" = יַגְשִׁים [equivalent] ↔ מְטַר אַרְצְךָ (דברים כח:כד) מָטָר / הִמְטִיר kept out.
dišpu; matāqu דְּבַשׁ; מָתַק [cognate]
tinūru תַּנּוּר [cognate]
rēmu; gimlu "mercy"; gamālu "spare"; gimilla turru "requite, avenge" רַחֲמִים; חֶמְלָה; חָמַל; הֵשִׁיב גְּמוּל (part 3, ll. 256–259; הָשֵׁב גְּמוּל, תהלים צד:ב) [cognate] (rēmu = רחם) ↔ וְנָתַן לְךָ רַחֲמִים (דברים יג:יח); [equivalent] (gamālu ~ גמל, Heb. "requite") ↔ וְלֹא תַחְמֹל (דברים יג:ט)
mūtānu; šaggaštu מַגֵּפָה; טֶבַח [equivalent] ↔ יַדְבֵּק יְהוָה בְּךָ אֶת הַדָּבֶר (דברים כח:כא) דֶּבֶר kept out (Deut's word).
huhāru; gišparru; tubāqu; kippu רֶשֶׁת; פַּח (2026-10-23 harmonization, was מְצוּדָה, EST 650); מְצוֹדָה (2026-10-23 harmonization row 21, was פַּח, EST 582); מַלְכֹּדֶת [equivalent] ↔ וּפָרַשְׂתִּי עָלָיו רִשְׁתִּי וְנִתְפַּשׂ בִּמְצוּדָתִי (יחזקאל יז:כ) gišparru = פח across the corpora (Etana, Maqlû, the Šamaš Hymn); tubāqu takes מְצוֹדָה (EST 582), so the treaty's trap words stay apart ([equivalent] Eccl 9:12 בִּמְצוֹדָה … בַּפָּח); shared with Maqlû's ḫuḫāru (another corpus).
qaštu; šebēru קֶשֶׁת; שָׁבַר [cognate] ↔ וְשָׁבַרְתִּי אֶת קֶשֶׁת (הושע א:ה)
rābiṣu (a demon "who lies in wait") רוֹבֵץ [cognate] ↔ לַפֶּתַח חַטָּאת רֹבֵץ (בראשית ד:ז) Always with a note.
šēdu רוּחַ־מָגֵן ≠ שֵׁד (false friend, creation corpus) Also where it is listed among evil demons (EST l. 493): the note says so.
utukku אוּטוּקּוּ (a kind of demon; note)

5. Law terms shared by the law collections (fixed 2026-10-17 by the coordinator, before drafting project 2, the Laws of Hammurabi)

Binding for projects 2 and 3 (LH, Eshnunna, MAL, Lipit-Ištar, Ur-Namma). LH's own formulas: 2-חוקי-חמורבי/renderings.md.

Akkadian Hebrew Rejected Echo Reason
šumma (protasis of a case law), u šumma אִם, וְאִם כִּי for the main case [equivalent] ↔ the casuistic כִּי / אִם of the Covenant Code (וְהִכָּה אִישׁ אֶת רֵעֵהוּ (שמות כא:יח), then אִם יָקוּם (שמות כא:יט)) One particle for one particle. The Covenant Code's two-tier system (כי for the main case, אם for its sub-cases) is a feature of the Torah's own drafting; imposing it on LH would hide that.
awīlum (law collections) אִישׁ; mār awīlim = בֶּן אִישׁ, mārat awīlim = בַּת אִישׁ, aššat awīlim = אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ, warad awīlim = עֶבֶד אִישׁ אָדָם (the narrative default of the flood and creation corpora; בן אדם would mean "a human being" and hide the class); בֶּן־חוֹרִין (an interpretation) [equivalent] ↔ אִישׁ of the case laws (שמות כא:יב, יד, טז, כ); בְּנֵי אִישׁ "the high-born" (תהלים מט:ג; סב:י) Deviation from the flood and creation corpora (awīlu = אָדָם), for the laws: awīlum is the legal person and the upper free class; בן איש keeps the class visible.
muškēnum מִסְכֵּן (always vocalized at the first occurrence in a file) עָנִי, דַּל (Hebrew poverty terms with their own Torah laws); הֶדְיוֹט (Mishnaic, Greek); transliteration [cognate loan] ↔ מִסְכֵּן (קהלת ד:יג; ט:טו–טז) The Hebrew word comes from this Akkadian one. Note: a status ("commoner, palace dependent"), not "pitiable" (modern Hebrew trap). Open decision for the user.
wardum; amtum עֶבֶד; אָמָה שִׁפְחָה for amtum [equivalent]; [cognate] (amtu = אָמָה)
iddâk (N of dâku) יֵהָרֵג (pl. יֵהָרְגוּ); G impersonal idukkūšu יַהַרְגוּהוּ יוּמַת, מוֹת יוּמָת [equivalent] ↔ מוֹת יוּמָת (שמות כא:יב, טו–יז; כב:יח) Corpus §2 dâku = הָרַג. The Torah's emphatic מוֹת יוּמָת has no Akkadian counterpart: the difference must be visible.
maḫar ilim; ina bīt ilim לִפְנֵי הָאֵל; בְּבֵית הָאֵל אֶל הָאֱלֹהִים [equivalent] ↔ אֶל הָאֱלֹהִים (שמות כא:ו; כב:ז–ח) Corpus ilu = אֵל, never אֱלֹהִים.
dīnum; dayyānum; dīnam dânu; dīnātum דִּין; דַּיָּן; דָּן דִּין; דִּינִים (dīnāt mīšarim דִּינֵי מֵישָׁרִים) מִשְׁפָּט (Akkadian šipṭu / šapāṭu is the cognate of שׁפט: reserve מִשְׁפָּט for it) [cognate] ↔ וְדַיַּן אַלְמָנוֹת (תהלים סח:ו); [equivalent] ↔ וְאֵלֶּה הַמִּשְׁפָּטִים (שמות כא:א) Corpus §2.
mīšarum; kittum מֵישָׁרִים; אֱמֶת צְדָקָה, צֶדֶק (for ṣidqu / ṣadāqu only) [cognate] מֵישָׁרִים ↔ מֵישָׁרִים מִשְׁפָּט וּצְדָקָה (תהלים צט:ד) Corpus §2.
šībū "witnesses"; šībūtum "testimony" עֵדִים; עֵדוּת [equivalent] ↔ עַל פִּי שְׁנֵי עֵדִים (דברים יט:טו) šību is literally "elder, grey-haired" (שָׂב): note at the first occurrence. In LH there is no adê, so עֵדוּת here is only "testimony".
kīma in the "X for X" clauses (alpam kīma alpim, wardam kīma wardim) כְּ־ (שׁוֹר כְּשׁוֹר) תַּחַת [equivalent] ↔ עַיִן תַּחַת עַיִן (שמות כא:כד); שׁוֹר תַּחַת הַשּׁוֹר (שמות כא:לו) Keep the Akkadian "like"; the Torah's "in place of" is its own. LH's eye-for-eye laws (§196–200) have no kīma at all: "they shall blind his eye".
nakāpu "gore"; nakkāpû "habitual gorer" נָגַף; נַגָּף (always vocalized) נָגַח, נַגָּח [cognate] ↔ וְכִי יִגֹּף שׁוֹר (שמות כא:לה); [equivalent] ↔ שׁוֹר נַגָּח הוּא (שמות כא:כט) The real cognate is the Torah's own verb in 21:35.
šūdû (Š of edû "know") "make known, notify" הוֹדִיעַ הֵעִיד, הוּעַד [cognate] (ידע); [equivalent] ↔ וְהוּעַד בִּבְעָלָיו (שמות כא:כט)
bēl + noun (owner) בַּעַל + noun אֲדוֹן [cognate] ↔ וּבַעַל הַשּׁוֹר (שמות כא:כח), בַּעַל הַבַּיִת (שמות כב:ז) bēlum "lord, master" (of persons) stays אָדוֹן (corpus §0).

6. Projects 3–6: the other law collections (fixed 2026-10-18 by the coordinator, before drafting)

Binding for Eshnunna (LE, project 3), the Middle Assyrian Laws A (MAL, project 4), Lipit-Ištar (LI, 5) and Ur-Namma (UN, 6), on top of §5 and of LH's fixed formulas (2-חוקי-חמורבי/renderings.md §1–§2, §4). Rule: an Akkadian legal formula that LH has gets LH's Hebrew, letter for letter (checked by laws_verify.py, which compares every identical normalization with LH and the other projects); a Sumerian formula gets the Hebrew of its standard Akkadian equivalent (Sum. tukum-bi = šumma = אִם; la₂ "weigh" = šaqālu = ישקול; gaz = dâku = יהרג; su(g) "replace" = riābu = יחליף; ra "strike" = maḫāṣu = מחץ). Look up any word with python3 -I laws_lookup.py '<regex>' before fixing it.

6.3 The Sumerian laws (Lipit-Ištar, Ur-Namma; projects 5–6)

Each Sumerian legal formula takes the Hebrew of its standard Akkadian equivalent (so that the same law in the two languages reads the same), and the Sumerian conventions of the earlier corpora (guidelines §5, Sumerian; סיפורי-המבול-המסופוטמיים/3-…, סיפורי-הבריאה-המסופוטמיים/2-…): marû = Hebrew future in the apodoses ("he shall pay"), ḫamṭu = past in the protases; ePSD2 lemma and morph in the פירוק field.

7. The Hittite texts: the Laws (project 8) and the Instructions for Temple Personnel (project 9) (fixed 2026-10-24 by the Round 4 run 6 coordinator, before drafting)

Binding for every Hittite text of the folder (tools/hittite_tools.py keys HL1, HL2, HLPT, IN) and, for the tables
§H2–§H9, for the Hittite rituals too (../טקסי-שילוח-וטיהור/): the tool reads the H-tables of both corpus files. The
translator brief is translator-brief--hittite.md (grammar mapping, ★ rules). The cuneiform law collections' binding
rules (§5–§6) hold for the Hittite Laws: one particle for one particle (takku = אִם), the class terms visible, the
small words where the laws differ from the Torah kept as the Hittite has them. Hittite is not Semitic: its contacts with
Hebrew are Sumerograms and Akkadograms (translated by the word they write, guidelines §6.3) and a few shared loanwords;
every overlap with the Torah is therefore an [equivalent], a [divergence] or an [absent], never a [cognate] (except
through an Akkadogram, which is the Akkadian word: say so).

    "corral" (ḫāli anda tarnatteni 7.5; ḫaliyaz ašaunaz 19.4) = מִכְלָאָה (HL1 precedent, with ašawar דִּיר). LÚ
    ḫaliyattalla-     "watchman" = שׁוֹמֵר; LÚ weḫeškattalla- "patrolman" and weḫ(ešk)- "patrol" = סוֹבֵב / יְסוֹבְבוּ
    (↔ הַשֹּׁמְרִים הַסֹּבְבִים בָּעִיר, שיר השירים ג:ג, in the apparatus only); paḫš- "guard" = שָׁמַר; the formula
    paḫḫaššanuwanteš ešten "be on your guard" = הֱיוּ נִשְׁמָרִים (F16; ↔ וְנִשְׁמַרְתֶּם מְאֹד, דברים ד:טו).
  • naḫḫanteš ešten "be fearful, reverent" (eight times, with mekki "much", marri) = הֱיוּ יְרֵאִים (F12): naḫḫ-
    is the Hittite counterpart of Akk. palāḫu, which holds ירא in every corpus; ↔ וּמִקְדָּשִׁי תִּירָאוּ (ויקרא יט:ל).
    ירא is gated (H4) to naḫḫ-; the homograph יראו "they will see" is not written (uškanzi = רוֹאִים).
  • SAG.DU-aš waštul "a sin of the head" (a capital offence; seven times) = חֵטְא־רֹאשׁ (F13; waštul חֵטְא,
    SAG.DU רֹאשׁ, §7.1); SAG.DU-aš ÚŠ-tar / akkatar "death of the head" = מוֹת־רֹאשׁ (F14). ↔ לָשֵׂאת חֵטְא לָמוּת
    (במדבר יח:כב), וְלֹא יִשְׂאוּ עָלָיו חֵטְא וּמֵתוּ בוֹ (ויקרא כב:ט): in the apparatus.
  • kartimmiya- / TUKU.TUKU-(nu-) "anger, make angry" = the root זעם (HL1 precedent: יזעמו); the Torah's הִכְעִיס
    (דברים ד:כה) is reserved (H3).
  • ḫuelpi "the young, fresh (produce, animal)" = הַטָּרִי (by meaning), never בִּכּוּרִים / רֵאשִׁית / בְּכוֹר
    (reserved, H3: ↔ שמות כג:יט, ויקרא כג:יד in the apparatus).
  • NINDA.GUR₄.RA UD-MI "the daily thick bread" = לֶחֶם עָבֶה יוֹמִי (or as the translator fixes it once); לֶחֶם הַתָּמִיד,
    לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים reserved (במדבר ד:ז). {DUG}išpantuzzi "libation vessel" = כְּלִי־נֶסֶךְ (נסך gated to išpant- /
    šipant-).
  • SANGA GAL / TUR = כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל / קָטָן ([equivalent] ↔ הַכֹּהֵן הַגָּדוֹל, ויקרא כא:י); GUDU₁₂ מְשׁוּחַ
    (always vocalized; הַכֹּהֵן הַמָּשִׁיחַ stays the Torah's); MUNUS AMA.DINGIR-LIM אֵם הָאֵל (always vocalized: unvocalized
    אם האל reads "if the god"; trap H6).
  • EZEN₄ "festival" = חַג; ḫamešḫa(nt)- אָבִיב (HL1), zena- סְתָו. DINGIR.MEŠ-aš ZI "the gods' soul / will" = נֶפֶשׁ הָאֵלִים (ZI נֶפֶשׁ, above); the translator fixes the phrase with the preposition once and keeps it.
  • Further reserved (H3), the Bible's words of the comparison (Lev 22:10, 18; Deut 23:22; Mal 3:8; Deut 4:25): תּוֹשָׁב,
    גֵּר, נֶדֶר, מִזְבֵּחַ, מַעֲשֵׂר, תְּרוּמָה, קָבַע, הִכְעִיס.

F4 parna=šš[eē]=a šuw\|parnašš?[eēi][iy]?a šuw ואל ביתו יביט "and he looks to his house"
F5 ^n=aš aki$\|^naš aki$ וימות "and he dies" (the case's second clause)

F7 \bḫurkel\b\|\bḫurk[ei]l\b תועבה
F8 ^(?:\S+ ){0,6}p[āa]i$ (?:^\| )ו?י?יתן(?: \|$)\|(?:^\| )ו?תיתן(?: \|$)\|(?:^\| )ו?יתנו(?: \|$) pāi "he gives" closing a clause = ייתן – the law formula [keys: HL1 HL2 HLPT] (scoped at the Round 5 finalization, 2026-11-02: elsewhere pāi is also the imperative "give!" (KU 126, HE 4:44, 22:9, AM 117–118) and the narrative present נותן (AP 1:17–19); IN has no clause-final pāi)

F11 \b(?:ul\|natta) ḫaratar\b אין(?: זו)? עברה UL / natta ḫaratar "it is no offence" = אֵין עֲבֵרָה (HL2, the sexual laws; §7.1)
F12 naḫḫanteš\|na-aḫ-ḫa-an-te-eš יראים naḫḫanteš ešten "be fearful" = הֱיוּ יְרֵאִים (IN)

F16 paḫ(?:ḫa)?(?:š\|šša)nu(?:w)?ant\|pa-aḫ-(?:ḫa-aš-)?ša-nu נשמרים paḫḫaššanuwanteš ešten "be on your guard" = הֱיוּ נִשְׁמָרִים (IN)
